$comment: Advisories that do NOT gate CI, with a written justification and a hard expiry.
Adding an entry here is a deliberate, reviewable act — never a silent suppression.
Rules enforced by scripts/audit-gate.mjs:
- An entry suppresses ONLY the named advisory in the named workspace.
- EVERY advisory id on a node needs its OWN entry (#2397). A package can carry
several; covering one no longer covers the rest. This was previously an
ANY-match, and `tmp` shipped for months with a HIGH advisory riding in on an
entry written for a LOW one that would not have gated by itself.
- There is NO package-name fallback. An entry is matched by its GHSA id and
nothing else, so an entry cannot silently widen to cover a re-issued or
newly-published advisory on the same package.
- Past `expires` the entry STOPS suppressing and the gate goes red, forcing a
re-review. Bump the date only with a fresh justification.
- An entry that no longer matches any advisory is reported as stale (warning),
so cleanup is prompted once upstream ships a fix.
- A node reported ONLY because it depends on something vulnerable (a path node
with no GHSA of its own) is cleared by the entry naming the package that
actually CARRIES the advisory, however deep the chain (#2388). Never add an
entry naming a package that is not itself vulnerable.
Only ever allowlist something that is genuinely not exploitable in this app.
'It is inconvenient to upgrade' is not a justification.

allow.reason: RSC-mode-only CSRF bypass. Darkwatch is a Vite SPA using react-router in DECLARATIVE mode (BrowserRouter + Routes/Route); it does not use React Server Components. Verified no RSC surface exists in client/src: no unstable_RSC, createCallServer, RSCHydratedRouter, and no @vitejs/plugin-rsc dependency. The vulnerable code path is therefore unreachable in this application. No fix is available on the React 18 line: react-router 7.18.1 is the last 7.x and is in the vulnerable range, while every 8.x release requires React >=19.2.7. Clearing this properly means a React 18 -> 19 upgrade, tracked in the issue above.

Dev-only, and NO upstream fix exists. extract-zip@2.0.1 is the LATEST published release (2023) and the advisory range is <=2.0.1, so there is nothing to upgrade or override to. Single path into this repo: @lhci/cli@0.15.1 -> lighthouse -> puppeteer-core -> @puppeteer/browsers -> extract-zip, where it unpacks browser archives fetched over HTTPS from Google's CDN -- not attacker-supplied zips, which is what the symlink-traversal advisory needs. npm's fixAvailable is @lhci/cli@0.1.0 flagged isSemVerMajor: a DOWNGRADE to a 2019-era Lighthouse CI that would break the lighthouse jobs to silence this -- the same trap as the tmp and js-yaml entries above. The root workspace has zero runtime dependencies ("dependencies": {}), so nothing here reaches the production image or a user; this code runs only when Lighthouse CI does. Clearing it properly means dropping @lhci/cli -- tracked in the issue above. This ONE entry now covers the whole chain: since #2388 audit-gate.mjs walks the `via` chain transitively, so lighthouse, puppeteer-core and @puppeteer/browsers -- none of which carry an advisory of their own -- are cleared by this entry instead of by three padding entries naming non-vulnerable packages.

The SECOND advisory on the same extract-zip node as GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv above, and un-suppressed only because #2397 requires one entry per advisory id rather than per package -- deliberately, since a package can carry several and covering one must not silently cover the rest. Same class (unvalidated symlink path traversal), same single path into this repo (@lhci/cli -> lighthouse -> puppeteer-core -> @puppeteer/browsers -> extract-zip), and the same reason it is unreachable here: extract-zip only unpacks browser archives fetched over HTTPS from Google's CDN during a Lighthouse CI run, never an attacker-supplied zip, which is what a symlink-traversal advisory needs. NO upstream fix exists -- extract-zip@2.0.1 (2023) is the latest published release and the advisory range is <=2.0.1, so there is nothing to upgrade or override to; npm's only offered fix is a semver-major DOWNGRADE of @lhci/cli that would break the lighthouse jobs. The root workspace has zero runtime dependencies, so this never reaches the production image or a user. Clearing it properly means dropping @lhci/cli, tracked in the issue above. Expiry matches its sibling so both come up for re-review together.

Crafted-input infinite loop in image-size's ICNS/JXL/HEIF parsers; no fixed release exists upstream (fixAvailable: none). Made unreachable in this app by magic-byte gating BEFORE imageSize at both call sites: imageProcessing.ts already restricted uploads to png/jpeg/webp via fileTypeFromBuffer, and imageProbe.ts (the DM-supplied-URL path, the one reachable with attacker bytes) now applies the same buffer-sniffing gate (png/jpeg/webp/gif) — the content-type header is attacker-controlled and is deliberately not trusted. Unit test pins the ICNS case. Upstream fix tracked in the issue above; on expiry, re-review or replace the dependency.
